papers.title: In situ calibration of microwave attenuation and gain using a cryogenic on-chip attenuator
papers.abstract: Accurate in situ calibration of microwave attenuation and amplification-chain noise is essential for superconducting quantum circuits. We demonstrate a compact, self-calibrating cryogenic noise source based on an on-chip chromium attenuator that can be resistively heated with nanowatt-level power and directly integrated into a coaxial microwave line at the mixing-chamber stage. By comparing Johnson-Nyquist noise generated by Joule and microwave heating, measured through the amplification chain, the attenuation of the input line, and hence the gain of the chain, is determined without requiring knowledge of the attenuator temperature. The device exhibits millisecond-scale response times and negligible heating of the cryostat base plate. Using this approach, we determine the gain and added noise of a cryogenic amplification chain over the 4-8 GHz band. Our results provide a simple and accurate method to characterize near-quantum-limited parametric amplifiers used in superconducting-qubit readout.

summary.summary: A compact cryogenic noise source based on a chromium on-chip attenuator heated with nanowatt-level DC power enables in situ calibration of microwave drive-line attenuation and amplifier noise by comparing Johnson–Nyquist noise generated via Joule and RF heating. The method determines input-line attenuation to ±0.5 dB over 4–8 GHz with millisecond thermal response times and negligible cryostat perturbation, yielding 23.6 ± 2.8 photons of added noise and 70.2 ± 0.5 dB gain for a HEMT-based readout chain.
summary.motivation: Accurate in situ characterization of drive-line attenuation and amplifier gain/noise temperature is essential for superconducting-qubit experiments, but existing cryogenic calibration methods either work only over narrow frequency bands, require complex modifications to wiring, or suffer from slow thermal response times on the order of minutes.
summary.method: A 60 nm chromium attenuator in T-network configuration on sapphire is resistively heated via a four-probe bias-tee connection at the mixing chamber and thermally isolated from the rest of the circuit via superconducting niobium leads; attenuation is extracted by least-squares fitting of power spectral density measurements comparing Joule heating to RF heating across the signal power range −22.5 to −5 dBm where the on-chip attenuator dominates noise generation.
summary.result: At 5.5 GHz, the method yields input-line attenuation of 76.3 ± 1 dB (validated against independent thermometer measurement), with thermal time constants of 0.25 ms (heating) and 1.57 ms (cooling), and characterizes the amplification chain as having 70.2 ± 0.5 dB gain and 23.6 ± 2.8 photons of system noise referenced to the noise-source output.

papers.title: Near-single-domain superconducting aluminum films on GaAs(111)A with exceptional crystalline quality for scalable quantum circuits
papers.abstract: We have reproducibly grown near-single-domain superconducting aluminum (Al) films on GaAs(111)A wafers using molecular beam epitaxy. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction revealed twin-domain ratios of 0.00005 and 0.0003 for 19.4-nm- and 9.6-nm-thick films, respectively-the lowest reported for Al on any substrate and long considered unattainable for practical device platforms. Azimuthal scans across off-normal Al{$11\bar{1}$} reflections exhibit narrow full width at half maximum (FWHM) values down to $0.55^\circ$, unmatched by epi-Al grown by any other method. Normal scans showed a well-defined (111) orientation with pronounced Pendellösung fringes, and $θ$-rocking-curve FWHM values down to $0.018^\circ$; the former indicates abrupt film-substrate and oxide-film interfaces. Electron backscatter diffraction mapping confirms macroscopic in-plane uniformity and the absence of $Σ$3 twin domains. Atomic force microscopy and scanning transmission electron microscopy confirmed atomically smooth surfaces and abrupt heterointerfaces. The films exhibit critical temperatures approaching bulk values, establishing a materials platform for scalable, high-coherence superconducting qubits.

summary.summary: Superconducting Al films grown on GaAs(111)A by molecular beam epitaxy achieve record-low twin-domain ratios of $5 	imes 10^{-5}$ to $3 	imes 10^{-4}$ and azimuthal rocking-curve FWHM down to $0.55°$, establishing a near-single-domain platform. Critical temperatures approach bulk values with atomically abrupt interfaces and macroscopic in-plane uniformity confirmed by synchrotron X-ray diffraction, EBSD, and STEM.
summary.motivation: Al superconducting qubits require exceptional crystalline quality to minimize decoherence, but twin-domain defects in epitaxial Al films degrade coherence and have historically limited practical integration on semiconductor platforms.
summary.method: Molecular beam epitaxy was used to grow Al on GaAs(111)A, with crystalline quality assessed via synchrotron X-ray diffraction (twin-domain ratios, rocking curves with FWHM to $0.018°$), electron backscatter diffraction mapping, and cross-sectional STEM characterization of interfaces.
summary.result: Twin-domain ratios of $5 	imes 10^{-5}$ (19.4 nm thick) and $3 	imes 10^{-4}$ (9.6 nm thick) are the lowest ever reported for Al on any substrate, with critical temperatures near bulk and atomically smooth surfaces enabling a high-coherence qubit platform.

papers.title: Fault-tolerant preparation of arbitrary logical states in the cat code
papers.abstract: Preparing high-fidelity logical states is a central challenge in fault-tolerant quantum computing, yet existing approaches struggle to balance control complexity against resource overhead. Here, we present a complete framework for the fault-tolerant preparation of arbitrary logical states encoded in the four-legged cat code. This framework is engineered to suppress the dominant incoherent errors, including excitation decay and dephasing in both the bosonic mode and the ancilla via error detection. Numerical simulations with experimentally realistic parameters on a 3D superconducting cavity platform yield logical infidelities on the order of $10^{-4}$. A scaling analysis confirms that the logical error rate grows nearly quadratically with the physical error rate, confirming that all first-order errors are fully suppressed. Our protocol is compatible with current hardware and is scalable to multiple bosonic modes, providing a resource-efficient foundation for magic state preparation and higher-level concatenated quantum error correction.

summary.summary: This work presents a fault-tolerant framework for preparing arbitrary logical states in the four-legged cat code using error-detectable operations in 3D superconducting cavities coupled to ancilla qubits. Numerical simulations achieve logical infidelities of $10^{-4}$ with quadratic suppression of first-order errors in photon loss and dephasing channels.
summary.motivation: Efficient high-fidelity logical state preparation is essential for magic state distillation and quantum error correction, yet existing approaches struggle to balance control complexity against resource overhead while suppressing dominant incoherent errors.
summary.method: The protocol engineers error-detectable coherent state discrimination $\mathcal{M}_{|\beta\rangle}$ through displacement, photon-number-selective ancilla flips, and reverse displacement, combined with parity measurement and existing error-detectable $Z_c(\theta)$ and $ZZ_c(\theta)$ rotations to realize a universal gate set $\{\mathcal{M}_P, Z_c(\theta), ZZ_c(\theta), \mathcal{M}_X, H_c\}$ on realistic 3D cavity-QED hardware.
summary.result: Two-qubit entangled state preparation achieves logical infidelity $(2.74 \pm 1.09) \times 10^{-4}$ at $\alpha = 2.9$ with $>95\%$ success probability; scaling analysis confirms $\bar{f}_L \propto s^{2.12 \pm 0.09}$, demonstrating first-order error suppression and robustness across a continuous family of target states.

papers.title: Fault-tolerant interfaces for quantum LDPC codes
papers.abstract: The preparation of a quantum state using a noisy quantum computer (gate noise strength $δ$), will necessarily affect an O($δ$)-fraction of the qubits, no matter which protocol is used. Here, we show that fault-tolerant quantum state preparation can be achieved with constant space overhead improving on previous constructions requiring polylogarithmic overhead. To achieve this, we add to the toolbox of fault-tolerant schemes for circuits with quantum input and output. More specifically, we construct fault-tolerant interfaces that decrease the level of protection for quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. When information is encoded in multiple code blocks, our interfaces have constant space overhead. In our decoder construction that change the level of protection by an arbitrary amount, we circumvent bottlenecks to error pileup and overhead by gradual lowering of the level of encoding at the same time as we increase the number of blocks on which decoding is carried out simultaneously.

summary.summary: This paper constructs fault-tolerant interfaces for quantum low-density parity-check codes that map encoded logical qubits to bare physical qubits with constant space overhead, improving on previous constructions requiring polylogarithmic overhead. The key innovation is a sequential procedure that gradually decreases the encoding level while increasing the number of code blocks in parallel, enabling constant-overhead fault-tolerant state preparation.
summary.motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires efficient schemes for state preparation, especially for resource state preparation in gate teleportation. Previous approaches using concatenated codes incur polylogarithmic overhead; this work aims to achieve constant overhead by leveraging recent advances in QLDPC codes.
summary.method: The construction combines partial decoding interfaces based on quantum teleportation with a novel sequentialization strategy that applies interfaces to a fraction of code blocks in parallel while performing error correction on remaining blocks, gradually transitioning from higher to lower encoding levels with decreasing circuit depth at each level.
summary.result: For QLDPC code families satisfying standard properties (constant rate $m_r \approx \alpha n_r$, linear minimum distance $d_\mathrm{min}(r) \geq \beta n_r$), the paper proves fault-tolerant state preparation with $O(x)$ qubit overhead for $x$-qubit outputs, with output noise bounded as local stochastic with parameter $(\kappa_1 \delta)^{\kappa_2}$ under circuit-level noise with strength $\delta < \delta_\mathrm{th}$.
